comment: GENERATED by tools/build_map.mjs — do not edit. The ground, on a grid, for the interface to draw as pixels. One letter per cell, indexed into `legend`; each row is run-length encoded as letter then count, where the count is left out for a run of one. Row 0 is the north. Cell centres are at originX + (x + 0.5) * cell and originY - (y + 0.5) * cell, in the same world units (kilometres) the province geometry uses, so the renderer needs no projection. Made again in projection B over the whole world to India by tools/welt_raster.py (13 October 2026): the old cells looked up through degrees, the new from Natural Earth. The window's edge is gone: the land runs on. Then tools/kuestenzellen.py (B098, 14 October 2026): a land cell no province reaches and the drawn coast puts wholly in the sea is made water. The coast of 1336 at the Jade and the Weser: the Jade Bight a small bay open to the North Sea, Arngast and the bight's south still land, Butjadingen an island behind the Ahne and the Heete by 1334 at the latest, the Weser an open funnel from Blexen and Lehe, the marsh without woods (the historiker, 19 October 2026). (tools/jade_weser.py) The reservoirs of the twentieth century given back to their valleys, the rivers running through them as lines, the provinces between them meeting on the river (the historiker, 20 October 2026; B118). (tools/stauseen_1336.py)
source: The provinces' own researched terrain inside the map; Natural Earth 1:10m (public domain) named landscapes, ranges, coastline and lakes outside it. Not an elevation model — see tools/build_map.mjs. See LICENSES.md.
